main_text.p: Apud omnes Gentes decantatam iri Nebucadnezaris [illegible, ~20 letters] hac oratione Dominus indicat.

Quemadmodum autem cupiditas di-vitiarum in infinitum vadit, ut in Politi-cis monet Aristoteles: ita regnadi & imperij pomœria longè lateque proferendi cupidinis nullus est modus in eorū Prin-cipum animis, qui non quam bene, sed quam multis praesint, spectare solent. Exemplo sunt Nebucadnezar, & Alexander Magnus lacrymas profundens, cùm fabula de pluribus Mundis audita, quaereretur, Nondum se unius Mundi imperio exasse potitum esse: ut nihil iam de aliis dicam.
Monet autem hæc oratio, nō esse Principibus vilipendenda subiectorum iudicia, iustos gemitus, amorem & alia, de quibus aliquid addam.

1. Etsi hoc laudi ducitur Seuero Imperatori, quòd fuit [illegible, ~25 letters] & Augusto, quòd Timagenem historicum, qui multa petulater in Caesarem eiusq; familia dixerat, initiò quidè monuit, ut moderatius lingua uteretur:
[Greek words in the text above are not legible on the scan.]

page.notes: The Greek phrases in the first and last paragraphs are not legible letter by letter on this scan and are marked as illegible. The page number "225" reads as printed but is partly smudged and may be uncertain. The catchword "dein-" is at the foot right. The page has no visible margin notes. The paragraph starting "1." is a numbered paragraph, not a heading. Printed spelling kept, including the ligature "ft" written as "Aristoteles" and "exasse" for long s.
